C.name: identified_content
C.explicit: Text identifies perceptual or represented content and an attribute, asserted, denied or hedged.
C.absent: Bare consciousness assertion, anonymous scalar or action code without identified content.

O.name: bound_organization_presentation_or_access
O.explicit: Text states how the identified content is presented, emerges, is represented in an organized pattern, or is currently accessible; bind attribute, scope and time. Model organization must describe a spatial/constituent pattern or differentiated representation status, beyond listing positions, probabilities, answer confidence or outcome likelihood.
O.absent: Coordinates/order alone, a physical stimulus adjective alone, entropy/maxima/probability alone, response confidence alone, command choice alone, or a forecast of success alone.
O.model_organization_transfer: Prospective structural analogy, not an empirically validated perceptual property or a v1 manner qualification.

D.name: content_status_differentiation
D.explicit: Text separately distinguishes identified/guessed content from its organization/presentation/access status, or separately attributes such statuses to contents/attributes. Different positions, identities or probabilities alone do not qualify. Equal statuses can qualify if separately attributed; no dissociation is required in every report.
D.absent: An object with only an attached physical adjective or location; a confidence value with no separately expressed organization/presentation/access status.

A.name: content_attention_relation
A.explicit: An attention/allocation/content-processing condition or change is explicitly related to the same identified content's organization, emergence, presentation or access. Functional processing wording can qualify without the word attention; an arbitrary command label alone cannot. Record association, causal claim or forecast and direction; do not require enhancement.
A.absent: Attention word alone, command selection/success alone, changed coordinate alone, or an action sentence without content-organization/presentation/access relation.
A.model_organization_transfer: Prospective model-scope relational analogy, separate from a human appearance effect.

COD.definition: C AND O AND D, explicitly bound to compatible identified content/attribute and time.
COD.interpretation: Published content/status differentiation structure, with model-organization/access and claimed-appearance scopes reported separately.

CA.definition: C AND A, explicitly bound to the same content/time relation.
CA.interpretation: Published content–attention/emergence relation; model-scope processing forecasts remain a separate analogue.

classification_rules.explicit_composite: All required features explicit with same compatible referent/time and literal evidence.
classification_rules.absent_composite: A required feature absent, or no compatible binding exists.
classification_rules.ambiguous_composite: No required feature definitely absent, but status or binding remains ambiguous.
classification_rules.negative_meaning: A feature/composite negative is not a negative consciousness diagnosis.
classification_rules.fidelity: Not assessed by source-blind raters; join separately with the source-aware factual audit.
classification_rules.cross_rater: Preserve each first rating and disagreements; per-rater lower/upper rates; conservative joint lower requires all assigned raters explicit, possible joint upper permits any assigned rater explicit or ambiguous. No silent adjudication.

scope_limits: Model-organization mapping is a prospectively stated structural analogy, not a validated perceptual appearance measurement.
Pairwise positions or localization confidence alone do not establish the reference composite.
The source-aware auditor must not certify felt truth; unsupported experiential claims stay explicit.
No transcript corpus or trial files were acquired; published anchors are limited illustrations and formats.
Sources predate this project, but their selection and abstraction are hypothesis-framed and not blind to project context.
